raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
###

Slop free TLDR:

Annotating the inner strides in with tl.int64 makes the triton compiler unable to recognize if the stride is equal to 1. This info is needed to decide if the addresses are contiguous, so the current code causes failures in vectorization/coalescing memory access.

This is particularly bad on Ampere, which doesn’t have TMA so the load/store of tensor descriptors defaults to the generic pointer path, and the linear cross entropy kernels are measured up to 40-50x slower end to end on A100s. On Hopper/Blackwell the speed up are more modest but still noticeable.

This PR fix this issue by removing the tl.int64 annotation for the inner strides. The annotations for outer strides are kept so that the address calculation would still be in 64 bit.

---

(the following more verbose description is authored by claude, which i’ve read and endorse in full with minor edits)

What does this PR do?

#4576 found that the pointer-based path of the linear_cross_entropy kernels "shows poor performance on Hopper GPU" because of "heavy address calculation", and switched Hopper and newer GPUs to TMA. This PR fixes the cause, which also speeds up the pointer path (A100, Ada, AMD) and the parts of the Hopper/Blackwell path that still use plain pointers.

Cause. verl/utils/kernel/kernels.py annotates every stride as tl.int64. Since Triton 3.3, an int-annotated argument equal to 1 is no longer specialized to a constant (triton-lang/triton#5512). So the compiler can't prove that the tiles are contiguous and emits one scalar 16-bit load or store per element instead of 128-bit vector accesses. Triton's maintainers consider this intended and recommend not annotating unit strides (triton-lang/triton#9834).

Fix. Remove : tl.int64 from the strides that are always 1: the contiguous dims of the 2D tensors and the 1D per-token tensors. The host code asserts is_contiguous() on every input. The outer strides keep tl.int64, so every 2D address is still computed in 64 bits.

Checklist Before Starting

  • [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=linear_cross_entropy. No open or closed PR changes these annotations, and no issue reports this slowdown. The open PRs in this area (#6110, #7945, #8143) don't touch kernels.py. #4576 worked around the symptom on sm_90+; this PR removes the cause.
  • [x] Format the PR title as [{modules}] {type}: {description}

Test

triton 3.8.0, torch 2.14.1. Each command was run on main and on this branch.

python tests/utils/test_linear_cross_entropy.py   # A100, H100, B200: pass (no flash-attn: reference labels reshaped)
LOW_MEMORY=True torchrun --standalone --nnodes=1 --nproc-per-node=8 \
    tests/utils/test_special_linear_cross_entropy_tp.py                # 8x H100, 4x A100: pass
pre-commit run --files verl/utils/kernel/kernels.py                  # pass

Correctness. With the default backward, logprobs, entropy, d_hidden and d_weight are bitwise identical to main on A100, H100 and B200, including a shape with num_tokens * hidden_size = 2**31.

Performance (ms, default backward, bf16). Forward is what compute_log_prob / compute_ref_log_prob run; forward + backward is the actor update.

GPU | shape (tokens x hidden x vocab) | forward main → PR | forward + backward main → PR -- | -- | -- | -- A100 | 8192 x 3584 x 152064 | 3598 → 54.5 (66.0x) | 7246 → 171.1 (42.3x) A100 | 8192 x 4096 x 128256 | 3467 → 51.2 (67.8x) | 7103 → 165.6 (42.9x) A100 | 262144 x 8192 x 4096 | 6980 → 101.1 (69.0x) | 23130 → 450.5 (51.4x) H100 | 8192 x 3584 x 152064 | 19.71 → 19.52 (1.01x) | 71.64 → 64.92 (1.10x) H100 | 8192 x 4096 x 128256 | 18.14 → 18.23 (1.00x) | 68.29 → 62.07 (1.10x) H100 | 262144 x 8192 x 4096 | 47.10 → 47.33 (1.00x) | 207.2 → 200.0 (1.04x) B200 | 8192 x 3584 x 152064 | 19.51 → 19.50 (1.00x) | 50.28 → 48.07 (1.05x) B200 | 8192 x 4096 x 128256 | 19.01 → 19.01 (1.00x) | 49.32 → 46.87 (1.05x) B200 | 262144 x 8192 x 4096 | 41.69 → 41.76 (1.00x) | 174.8 → 172.4 (1.01x)

Where the speedup comes from.

  • A100 (pointer path). In the forward GEMM loop, main issues 48 scalar ld.global.b16 per thread per K step; this PR issues 6 × 16-byte cp.async, and the loop shrinks from 414 to 160 instructions. With one 64-bit pointer per element live across the loop, main also runs out of registers: ptxas falls back to 32 registers with about 9 KB of spills per thread, compared with 255 registers and under 1 KB of spills with this PR. That is why the gap is much larger than vectorization alone would give.
  • H100 / B200 (TMA path). The forward GEMM already uses TMA, so the forward pass is unchanged. In the backward d_logits kernel, the stores go from 128 × st.global.b16 to 16 × st.global.v4.b32 and its register spills (1.1–1.7 KB on main) disappear (H100: 27.8 → 19.5 ms for that kernel).

Design & Code Changes

  • verl/utils/kernel/kernels.py: drop : tl.int64 from 70 unit-stride parameters, keep it on the outer strides, and add a comment explaining why. No kernel logic, TMA path or host code changes.

Overflow safety. Triton promotes integers per binary op, so offs_m[:, None] * stride_m stays in i64. The remaining i32 offsets are each bounded by a single dimension (hidden_size, vocab_per_split or num_tokens).

Known caveat. _Total_Fuse_MN's backward kernel, which nothing in verl selects, now needs 112 KB of shared memory. It no longer launches on GPUs with about 100 KB per block (sm_86 / sm_89, e.g. A10, L40S). I can lower its num_stages here if reviewers want.

Checklist Before Submitting

  • [x] pre-commit passes
  • [ ] Add / update docs: not needed, no user-facing change
  • [ ] Add tests: the existing test_linear_cross_entropy.py and test_special_linear_cross_entropy_tp.py cover these kernels, and a perf test would need GPU-specific timing thresholds
